statement: Forked-owner counterbranch theorem. For every m>=3,r>=0, the minimal natural-switch state complex with two mutually exclusive alternatives wx1 and ux1 sharing owner cy1 has exact singleton kernel F_fork=R x ({x1} union Y) union {x1} x (X-{x1,x2}) union {y1,y2} x (Y-{y1,y2}) union K(Y-{y1,y2}); every trace has size one or three, F_fork hits every trace, and tau=r(m+1)+(m-2)(m+3)/2. Hence owner/state/trace-preserving reduction to the round-9 two-owner Boolean architecture is impossible without a new distinct-owner Booleanity hypothesis.
closes: constructs an exact all-parameter legal counterbranch to universality of the round-9 labelled architecture
identifies distinct-owner matching rank and Boolean joint compatibility as the missing reduction hypothesis
quantifies the exact kernel loss r+m-2 under the first owner collision
dependency_gaps: The forked family is not derived from every public hard branch and is not proved to be a floor(n^2/4)+1 threshold hard graph.
No theorem forces two distinct owners or a Boolean joint switch state from the canonical hardness normal form.
No output-expansion composition or improvement of the public 1/8 leading constant is supplied.
External novelty and priority are unchecked.
